itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Ollantaytambo – Km 104 – Wiñay Wayna – Inti Punku
itinerary.description: Very early pickup from your hotel in Cusco and transfer to the Ollantaytambo train station to board the scenic train to Km 104, the checkpoint where the official Inca Trail permit and each passenger's ID are verified. From there the hike begins (approx. 3 to 4 hours), crossing the Urubamba River and passing near the archaeological sites of Chachabamba and Choquesuysuy, climbing a cloud-forest trail lined with orchids up to the Wiñay Wayna complex. The route continues to Inti Punku (Sun Gate), where you get your first views of Machu Picchu before descending to Aguas Calientes for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Machu Picchu and return to Cusco
itinerary.description: Breakfast, then a ride up by tourist bus (or on foot) to the citadel of Machu Picchu for a guided tour of its main sectors, covering its history, architecture and significance within the Inca empire. Free time to explore on your own before heading back down to Aguas Calientes. In the afternoon, return by train to Ollantaytambo and then by tourist transport to Cusco.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Km 82 – Llactapata – Wayllabamba
itinerary.description: Early-morning pickup from your hotel in Cusco and transfer by bus to Ollantaytambo and then to Km 82, the checkpoint where the official Inca Trail permit and each passenger's ID are verified. The hike begins by crossing a bridge over the Urubamba River and follows a mostly flat trail to Miskay, then climbs to the archaeological site of Llactapata, with views of the Verónica snow-capped peak. The route continues to Wayllabamba (approx. 3,000 m/9,840 ft), the first designated campsite, where the cook team prepares dinner.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Wayllabamba – Warmiwañusca (Dead Woman's Pass) – Pacaymayu
itinerary.description: Considered the most demanding day of the route: a steady climb up stone stairways and puna trails to Warmiwañusca, or Dead Woman's Pass, the highest point of the trail at approximately 4,200-4,215 m (13,780-13,830 ft). After taking in the panoramic mountain views, the trail descends to the Pacaymayu valley (around 3,600 m/11,810 ft), where the second designated campsite is set up and a hot dinner prepared by the cook team is served.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Pacaymayu – Runkurakay – Sayacmarca – Phuyupatamarca – Wiñay Wayna
itinerary.description: Considered the day richest in archaeology: a climb to the Runkurakay pass and site, followed by a descent to Sayacmarca through a rock-carved Inca tunnel. The trail continues to Phuyupatamarca ('town above the clouds'), with its agricultural terraces and views of the Vilcabamba mountain range, then descends a long stone stairway to the Wiñay Wayna complex, where the last designated campsite is set up, already within the cloud forest.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Wiñay Wayna – Inti Punku – Machu Picchu – return to Cusco
itinerary.description: Very early departure (before dawn) to the final Inca Trail checkpoint and an approximately 2-hour walk to Inti Punku (Sun Gate), from where, weather permitting, you get your first views of Machu Picchu at sunrise. Descent to the citadel for a guided tour of its main sectors. Free time before heading down to Aguas Calientes for lunch and boarding the return train to Ollantaytambo, connecting with tourist transport to Cusco.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Mollepata – Soraypampa
itinerary.description: Early-morning pickup from your hotel in Cusco and transfer by vehicle to Mollepata, where breakfast is served before continuing by road to the trailhead. A moderate ascent hike (approx. 3 hours) through the valley to Soraypampa, with views of the Salkantay snow-capped peak. Pack horses carry the shared luggage. Dinner and overnight at the Soraypampa campsite, at the foot of the mountain range.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Soraypampa – Salkantay Pass – Collpapampa
itinerary.description: A climb of approximately 3 to 4 hours from Soraypampa to the Salkantay Pass, the highest point of the route at around 4,600-4,650 m (15,090-15,255 ft), with close-up views of the Salkantay snow-capped peak. Lunch on the way down in the Huayracmachay area, followed by a noticeable change in landscape toward the cloud forest, descending several more hours to the Collpapampa campsite, already in warmer, more humid weather.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Collpapampa – Chaullay – Sahuayaco Beach – Hidroeléctrica – Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description: A hike through coffee plantations, tropical fruit orchards and cloud forest, passing through Chaullay and Sahuayaco Beach along the river. The trail continues to the Hidroeléctrica area, from where you walk (or take transportation, depending on operation) alongside the railway for approximately 2 hours to Aguas Calientes, where you spend the night at a lodging with a private bathroom.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Machu Picchu and return to Cusco
itinerary.description: Very early departure to the citadel of Machu Picchu (by tourist bus or on foot) for a guided tour of the sanctuary's main sectors. Free time to explore before heading down to Aguas Calientes for lunch. In the afternoon, return by train to Ollantaytambo and then by tourist transport to Cusco.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Tinki – Upis
itinerary.description: Very early pickup from your hotel in Cusco and transfer by vehicle (approx. 3-4 hours) to the community of Tinki, gateway to the Ausangate mountain range. Meeting with the horsemen and pack horse team, then start of the hike to Upis (around 4,400 m/14,435 ft), an area with natural hot springs and close-up views of the Ausangate snow-capped peak (6,384 m/20,945 ft). Dinner and first overnight at the designated campsite.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Upis – Arapa Pass – high-Andean lagoons – Ausangatecocha
itinerary.description: Climb to Arapa Pass (approx. 4,850-4,900 m/15,910-16,075 ft), with views of several turquoise-toned glacial lagoons such as Pukacocha, Hatun Pukacocha and Qomerqocha. Descent to the Ausangatecocha area, where camp is set up beside a lagoon fed by the mountain's meltwater. Frequent sightings of vicuñas, alpacas and high-Andean birds throughout the day.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Ausangatecocha – Palomani Pass – Pampacancha – Q'ampa
itinerary.description: The most demanding day of the circuit: a climb to Palomani Pass, at around 5,200 m (17,060 ft) and the highest point of the entire route, with panoramic views of the Vilcanota mountain range. Descent to Pampacancha, a grazing area for llamas and alpacas belonging to local communities, before continuing to the Q'ampa campsite.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Q'ampa – Andean pass – Pacchanta
itinerary.description: Crossing one last high Andean pass before starting the descent to Pacchanta, a community known for its natural hot springs at the foot of Ausangate. Free afternoon to relax in the thermal pools (entrance not included) and spend time with the local alpaca-herding community. Last overnight at the Pacchanta campsite.

itinerary.title: Day 5: Pacchanta – Tinki – return to Cusco
itinerary.description: A short hike (approx. 1-2 hours) from Pacchanta to Tinki, closing the circuit around the Ausangate snow-capped peak. Farewell lunch and return by tourist transport to Cusco, arriving in the late afternoon/evening.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Abra Málaga – bike descent – Santa María
itinerary.description: Very early pickup from your hotel in Cusco (between 6:00 and 6:30 a.m.) and drive through the highlands to Abra Málaga, at around 4,300-4,350 m (14,105-14,270 ft), with a breakfast stop in the Sacred Valley. From the pass, a multi-hour mountain bike descent begins along a paved and later gravel road, crossing ecological zones that shift from cold puna to cloud forest. Lunch along the way and arrival in the afternoon at Santa María, where you spend the night at basic hostel/lodge-style accommodation.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Santa María – Santa Teresa – zipline, hot springs and hike to Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description: Breakfast, then transfer to Santa Teresa for a zipline/canopy circuit over the valley (an optional activity with some operators). Free time to relax at the Cocalmayo hot springs. In the afternoon, a hike of around 2 to 3 hours alongside the railway to Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo), where you spend the night at simple lodging with a private bathroom, already within the cloud forest area.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Machu Picchu and return to Cusco
itinerary.description: Very early departure from Aguas Calientes by bus (or on foot, depending on preference) to the citadel of Machu Picchu for an approximately 2-hour guided tour of the sanctuary's main sectors. Free time to explore on your own before heading back down to Aguas Calientes. In the afternoon, return by train to Ollantaytambo and from there by tourist transport to Cusco, arriving at night.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Cusco – Abra Málaga – bike descent – rafting – Santa María
itinerary.description: Pickup from your hotel in Cusco between 6:00 and 6:30 a.m. and transfer through the Sacred Valley to Abra Málaga (approx. 4,300-4,350 m/14,105-14,270 ft), the starting point for a multi-hour mountain bike descent to the Santa María area, crossing different ecological zones. In the afternoon, for those who want it, an optional rafting session on moderate stretches of the Urubamba River (depending on river level and safety conditions). Dinner and overnight at basic lodge/hostel-style accommodation in Santa María.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Santa María – stretch of the original Inca trail – Santa Teresa
itinerary.description: Breakfast, then a hike along trails that include a stretch of the original Inca trail, through cloud-forest scenery, coffee, fruit and coca plantations. Visit to a local family and a brief coca-leaf ceremony following Andean custom. River crossing via a hand-pulled cable car (oroya) and arrival in Santa Teresa, where there is free time at the Cocalmayo hot springs in the afternoon. Overnight at simple accommodation in Santa Teresa.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Santa Teresa – zipline – hike to Aguas Calientes
itinerary.description: In the morning, a zipline/canopy activity over the Santa Teresa valley (several lines with views of the mountains and river). Transfer to the Hidroeléctrica area for lunch, then an approximately 2 to 3-hour hike alongside the railway to Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo). Dinner and overnight at lodging with a private bathroom, with an informative talk from the guide about the following day's visit to Machu Picchu.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Machu Picchu and return to Cusco
itinerary.description: Very early departure to the citadel of Machu Picchu (by tourist bus or on foot) for an approximately 2-hour guided tour of the main archaeological sectors. Free time for photos and further exploration before heading down to Aguas Calientes for lunch. In the afternoon, return by train to Ollantaytambo and then by tourist transport to Cusco, arriving at night.
